Question: Let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be circles defined by \[(x - 10)^2 + y^2 = 36\] and \[(x + 15)^2 + y^2 = 81,\] respectively. What is the length of the shortest line segment \(\overline{PQ}\) that is tangent to \(C_1\) at \(P\) and to \(C_2\) at \(Q?\)
Solution:
The circle equations give centers \(O_1=(10,0)\) and \(O_2=(-15,0)\), with radii \(6\) and \(9\). Thus \(O_1O_2=25\).

For any common tangent through \(P\) and \(Q\), the radii \(O_1P\) and \(O_2Q\) are perpendicular to the tangent. Draw through \(O_1\) a line parallel to the tangent until it meets the line \(O_2Q\). This forms a right triangle with hypotenuse \(25\) and one leg equal to \(PQ\).

If the centers lie on opposite sides of the tangent, the other leg is \(6+9=15\). If they lie on the same side, it is \(9-6=3\). These exhaust the possibilities, since a circle's center cannot lie on its tangent. The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
PQ=\begin{cases}
\sqrt{25^2-15^2}=20,&\text{opposite sides},\\
\sqrt{25^2-3^2}=\sqrt{616}>20,&\text{same side}.
\end{cases}
\]
To verify that the shorter case occurs, let \(O=(0,0)\). Since \(OO_1=10>6\), draw a tangent from \(O\) to \(C_1\). The perpendicular triangles from the two centers to this line are similar: they have right angles and equal angles at \(O\). Because \(OO_2/OO_1=15/10\), the distance from \(O_2\) to the line is
\[
\frac{15}{10}\cdot6=9.
\]
The line is therefore also tangent to \(C_2\). Its centers lie on opposite sides because \(O\) lies between them. Hence the shortest segment has length \(\boxed{20}\), choice C.
